definition: A degenerative process where a model trained repeatedly on data generated by earlier AI models (rather than diverse human-generated data) loses diversity and quality over successive generations.
details: Model collapse is a growing concern as more AI-generated content appears on the web and potentially gets swept into future training datasets, motivating interest in provenance tracking and careful data curation.
story: Imagine a new medicine that works brilliantly in the lab but still has to be tested on real people before anyone takes it. Think of it as the quiet rule that a tool should be useful without being dangerous. The idea is simple: before something powerful is let loose, someone checks that it will not do real harm to real people. Rules and red-teaming are the brakes that make the speed trustworthy. That deliberate caution is Model Collapse.
